body.en:
Question B-006-003-004.

Why the correct answer is right: RG-213 is a larger 50-ohm coax often used for high-frequency (HF) station runs. PL-259 connectors are commonly fitted to connect that cable to many HF transceivers.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "An F-type connector": F connectors are common on 75-ohm television and cable systems, not the usual RG-213-to-HF-transceiver connector.
- sourceIndex 2: "An SMA connector": SMA connectors are small threaded connectors seen on handhelds and compact gear; they are not the normal connector for large RG-213 HF cable.
- sourceIndex 3: "A BNC connector": BNC connectors are useful on test equipment and low-power gear, but PL-259 is the common answer for RG-213 on many HF transceivers.
